parts.article:
Katherine Mansfield
 
Katherine Mansfield was a modernist writer of short fiction who was born and brought up in New Zealand.
 
(A) Katherine Mansfield Beauchamp Murry was born in 1888, into a prominent family in Wellington, New Zealand. She became one of New Zealand's best-known writers, using the pen name of Katherine Mansfield. The daughter of a banker, and born into a middle-class family, she was also a first cousin of Countess Elizabeth von Arnim, a distinguished novelist in her time. Mansfield had two older sisters and a younger brother. Her father, Harold Beauchamp, went on to become the chairman of the Bank of New Zealand. In 1893, the Mansfield family moved to Karori, a suburb of Wellington, where Mansfield would spend the happiest years of her childhood; she later used her memories of this time as an inspiration for her Prelude story.
 
(B) Her first published stories appeared in the High School Reporter and the Wellington Girls' High School magazine in 1898 and 1899. In 1902, she developed strong feelings for a musician who played the cello, Arnold Trowell, although her feelings were not, for the most part, returned. Mansfield herself was an accomplished cellist, having received lessons from Trowell's father. Mansfield wrote in her journals of feeling isolated to some extent in New Zealand, and, in general terms, of her interest in the Maori people (New Zealand's native people), who were often portrayed in a sympathetic light in her later stories, such as How Pearl Button Was Kidnapped.
 
(C) She moved to London in 1903, where she attended Queen's College, along with her two sisters. Mansfield recommenced playing the cello, an occupation that she believed, during her time at Queen's, she would take up professionally. She also began contributing to the college newspaper, with such a dedication to it that she eventually became its editor. She was particularly interested in the works of the French writers of this period and in the 19th century British writer, Oscar Wilde, and she was appreciated amongst fellow students at Queen's for her lively and charismatic approach to life and work. She met fellow writer Ida Baker, a South African, at the college, and the pair became lifelong friends. Mansfield did not actively support the suffragette movement in the UK. Women in New Zealand had gained the right to vote in 1893.
 
(D) Mansfield first began journeying into other parts of Europe in the period 1903–1906, mainly to Belgium and Germany. After finishing her schooling in England, she returned to her New Zealand home in 1906, only then beginning to write short stories in a serious way. She had several works published in Australia in a magazine called The Native Companion, which was her first paid writing work, and by this time she had her mind set on becoming a professional writer. It was also the first occasion on which she used the pseudonym “K. Mansfield”. Mansfield rapidly grew discontented with the provincial New Zealand lifestyle, and with her family. Two years later she headed again to London. Her father sent her an annual subsidy of £100 for the rest of her life. In later years, she would express both admiration and disdain for New Zealand in her journals.
 
(E) In 1911, Mansfield met John Middleton Murry, the Oxford scholar and editor of the literary magazine Rhythm. They were later to marry in 1918. Mansfield became a co-editor of Rhythm, which was subsequently called The Blue Review, in which more of her works were published. She and Murry lived in various houses in England and briefly in Paris. The Blue Review failed to gain enough readers and was no longer published. Their attempt to set up as writers in Paris was cut short by Murry's bankruptcy, which resulted from the failure of this and other journals. Life back in England meant frequently changed addresses and very limited funds.
 
(F) Between 1915 and 1918, Mansfield moved between England and Bandol, France. She and Murry developed close contact with other well-known writers of the time such as D. H. Lawrence, Bertrand Russell and Aldous Huxley. By October 1918 Mansfield had become seriously ill; she had been diagnosed with tuberculosis and was advised to enter a sanatorium. She could no longer spend winters in London. In the autumn of 1918 she was so ill that she decided to go to Ospedaletti in Italy. It was the publication of Bliss and Other Stories in 1920 that was to solidify Mansfield's reputation as a writer. Mansfield also spent time in Menton, France, as the tenant of her father's cousin at “The Villa Isola Bella”. There she wrote eight stories including Miss Brill and The Daughters of the Late Colonel, the latter of which she pronounced to be “…the only story that satisfies me to any extent”.
 
(G) Mansfield produced a great deal of work in the final years of her life, and much of her prose and poetry remained unpublished at her death in 1923. After her death, her husband, Murry, took on the task of editing and publishing her works. His efforts resulted in two additional volumes of short stories, The Doves' Nest and Something Childish, published in 1923 and 1924 respectively; the publication of her Poems; as well as a collection of critical writings (Novels and Novelists) and a number of editions of Mansfield's previously unpublished letters and journals.

reference:
Q1

干扰 原文明确区分了“pen name（笔名）”和出生时的全名，长度都不一样，绝非“exactly the same”。

句子 (Paragraph A) “She became one of New Zealand's best-known writers, using the pen name of Katherine Mansfield... born... Katherine Mansfield Beauchamp Murry.”

解析 题目说她书上的名字和原名“完全一样（exactly the same）”，原文A段说她用笔名Katherine Mansfield，而原名是“Katherine Mansfield Beauchamp Murry”，显然不同，选 FALSE。

Q2

解析 原文B段只提到她的首批故事“发表（appeared）”在High School Reporter上，完全没有提及她是否因此“得奖（won a prize）”，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 “发表”不等于“获奖”，不要因为她是著名作家就默认她小时候一定得过奖。

句子 (Paragraph B) “Her first published stories appeared in the High School Reporter...”

Q3

解析 题目说《Pearl Button》这篇故事以“有利/正面（favourable）”的方式描绘毛利人。原文B段说毛利人在她后来的故事中常以“同情/好感的光环（sympathetic light）”被描绘，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Sympathetic light” 在文学批评中通常指带有同情、理解和好感的正面描写，对应 “favourable way”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...Maori people... who were often portrayed in a sympathetic light in her later stories, such as How Pearl Button Was Kidnapped.”

Q4

干扰 注意时间点“during her time at Queen's”，那时的目标是音乐（cello），不是写作。

解析 题目说她在Queen's College时计划成为职业作家。原文C段说她在那里时相信自己会职业从事“大提琴（playing the cello）”，成为职业作家是回新西兰后的事（1906年），选 FALSE。

句子 (Paragraph C) “Mansfield recommenced playing the cello, an occupation that she believed, during her time at Queen's, she would take up professionally.”

Q5

解析 题目说她在Queen's College不受其他学生欢迎（unpopular）。原文C段说她因活泼和魅力被同学“欣赏（appreciated）”，即受欢迎，选 FALSE。

干扰 “Appreciated amongst fellow students” 直接反驳了 “unpopular”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...she was appreciated amongst fellow students at Queen's for her lively and charismatic approach...”

Q6

解析 原文C段只说她“没有积极支持（did not actively support）”英国的妇女参政运动，但这不代表她对政治“几乎没兴趣（little interest）”，可能只是不支持该特定运动或方式，信息不充分，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 这道题有另外一个版本，原文对应答案句为“Mansfield did not become involved in much political activity when she liveed in London. For example, although at that time in London many women were demonstrating for votes for women, Mansfield did not actively support the suffragette movement in the UK...”，所以答案选 A。

句子 (Paragraph C) “Mansfield did not actively support the suffragette movement in the UK.”

Q7

句子 (Paragraph D) “...she returned to her New Zealand home in 1906...”

干扰 定位词“moved... back”对应原文的“returned”。

解析 题目问哪一年从英国搬回新西兰，原文D段提到“she returned to her New Zealand home in 1906”，填 1906。

Q8

解析 题目说第一份有偿写作是在总部位于____的出版物上，原文D段说作品发表在“Australia（澳大利亚）”的一本杂志上，这是她第一份有偿工作，填 Australia。

干扰 题目问的是地点“based in ______”，对应原文的“published in Australia”。

句子 (Paragraph D) “She had several works published in Australia... which was her first paid writing work...”

Q9

解析 题目说她的____和新西兰的生活方式让她感到不满，原文D段说她对新西兰生活方式以及“her family（她的家人）”感到不满，填 family。

干扰 并列连词“and”连接了“lifestyle”和“family”，直接定位。

句子 (Paragraph D) “Mansfield rapidly grew discontented with the provincial New Zealand lifestyle, and with her family.”

Q10

句子 (Paragraph E) “Their attempt... in Paris was cut short by Murry's bankruptcy...”

解析 题目说____阻止了二人在巴黎待在一起，原文E段说他们在巴黎的尝试被Murry的“bankruptcy（破产）”打断了，填 bankruptcy。

干扰 “Prevented... from staying” 对应原文的 “cut short”；导致这件事的原因是 bankruptcy。

Q11

解析 题目说花时间和杰出的____在一起，原文F段提到与当时其他著名的“writers（作家）”如劳伦斯等人建立了密切联系，填 writers。

干扰 “Distinguished” 对应原文的 “well-known”，填复数名词。

句子 (Paragraph F) “She and Murry developed close contact with other well-known writers of the time...”

Q12

解析 题目说随着《Bliss》出版，她的____被巩固了，原文F段说这本书的出版“solidify Mansfield's reputation（巩固了曼斯菲尔德的声誉）”，填 reputation。

干扰 动词“consolidated”是原文“solidify”的同义替换。

句子 (Paragraph F) “It was the publication of Bliss... that was to solidify Mansfield's reputation as a writer.”

Q13

解析 题目说曼斯菲尔德的____在她死后出版了更多作品，原文G段说她死后，她的“husband（丈夫）”Murry承担了编辑出版的任务，填 husband。

干扰 虽然原文也给了名字 Murry，但题目结构是“Mansfield's ______”，填身份词 husband 最为准确。

句子 (Paragraph G) “After her death, her husband, Murry, took on the task of editing and publishing her works.”
